assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of defect-mediated melting gave a powerful, general account of phase transitions in two dimensions and predicted the hexatic phase. Its conceptual reach across condensed matter and soft matter is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Halperin, Nelson, and Young are appropriately credited for the central theory and its development.
assessment.maturity: The framework has had decades of scrutiny and broad influence; its core conclusions are well established.
uncertainties: The boundaries of the original theory’s applicability depend on material-specific interactions and defects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov–Bohm effect and geometric phase revealed that quantum phase has observable consequences beyond local force fields. These ideas became foundational across quantum mechanics and many areas of physics.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov is central to the Aharonov–Bohm effect, while Berry’s general adiabatic phase concept established a broad and enduring framework.
assessment.maturity: Both effects and their many applications have been extensively confirmed and understood over decades.
uncertainties: The discovery combines distinct contributions from different periods, so the precise scope of a single prize citation would need care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction showed that quantum information can be protected against noise in principle, turning a major conceptual objection into a framework for fault-tolerant computation. Topological codes added a deep connection to phases of matter.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane introduced influential early codes, and Kitaev developed the topological-code approach; the proposed set captures distinct foundational contributions.
assessment.maturity: The theory is rigorous and experimentally tested in increasingly capable systems, though large-scale fault-tolerant operation remains unrealized.
uncertainties: The field has many major contributors, and a three-person attribution necessarily omits important work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory provided a tractable, physically transparent way to understand strongly correlated electrons, including the Mott transition. It is a remarkably useful framework linking analytic ideas with realistic materials.
assessment.attribution: Georges, Vollhardt, and Kotliar are central to developing and establishing the method and its applications.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been extensively developed and applied for decades, with a clear record of explanatory power.
uncertainties: Its single-site form neglects spatial correlations, so its reach is limited in some low-dimensional systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realizing strongly interacting Fermi gases and observing the BEC–BCS crossover created a clean experimental setting for universal quantum many-body physics. The work connected previously separated regimes of fermionic superfluidity.
assessment.attribution: The proposed laureates represent major experimental contributions to realizing and studying these gases and the crossover.
assessment.maturity: The systems and central phenomena have been studied extensively, with precise control and a mature body of results.
uncertainties: The discovery and subsequent mapping of the crossover involved several groups, making the boundaries of credit contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Gauge/gravity duality is a striking conceptual connection between quantum field theory and gravity, with broad influence on theoretical physics and useful tools for strongly coupled systems.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena proposed the concrete duality, and Witten helped clarify and develop its significance; their contributions are especially central to this formulation.
assessment.maturity: The correspondence is mathematically rich and extensively studied, but its physical status as a description of our universe remains untested.
uncertainties: There is no direct experimental confirmation, and the relation to observable quantum gravity is indirect.
The cited discovery has antecedents in earlier work on string theory and gauge dynamics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation offers an influential explanation for the early universe’s large-scale uniformity and the origin of primordial structure. The link between quantum fluctuations and observed cosmological structure is physically compelling.
assessment.attribution: Guth introduced the inflationary idea, Linde developed important models, and Mukhanov made foundational contributions to the theory of primordial perturbations.
assessment.maturity: The theory’s perturbation predictions are well integrated into modern cosmology, but inflation itself has not been uniquely established by observation.
uncertainties: Many inflationary models fit current data, and a decisive signature distinguishing them has not been observed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and message-passing theory brought statistical physics to random constraint-satisfaction problems and exposed rich glassy transitions in computation. This is a notable conceptual bridge between physics and computer science.
assessment.attribution: Mézard and Zecchina are strongly associated with the development and demonstration of these methods.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical framework and its influence are well established, though its status is more specialized than that of discoveries with broad experimental reach.
uncertainties: The method’s strongest results rely on assumptions about random ensembles that do not always carry over to practical instances.
